narrative.overview:
SSH Astra plays the category standard straight: the Termius / Warp / WindTerm workstation. A 48px nav rail on the far left, a Host vault (a 248px Host list column, and Home's grid of Host cards), compact pill tabs, Terminals that fill the stage with the File panel docked beside them, and a dense 24px status bar. Nothing about the layout tries to be novel; the craft is in density, alignment and state.

The identity is the theme model. Thirteen whole-window themes ship, and a theme is never just a Terminal scheme: it names the ground, sidebar, surface, raised layer, text, muted text, border, accent and state colours of the chrome *and* the Terminal's 16-colour palette, and every other token derives from those. Switching theme recolours the window and every open Terminal in one frame; hovering a theme in the gallery previews it live across the whole window before a click commits. Host monograms and tab marks take their colour from the active theme's ANSI hues, so each Host keeps a stable identity that still belongs to whatever theme is painted.

Density is desktop density: 13px body, 26px icon buttons, 28px tabs, 30px Host rows, 24px status bar. Light and dark are equal citizens; the default follows the OS appearance, with a separately chosen light theme and dark theme. The world replaces the earlier "lit sheet on a tinted desk" system: there is no grey desk with floating white sheets any more, and no single fixed palette.
keyCharacteristics: Thirteen whole-window themes; one theme paints chrome and Terminal together.
Twelve named roles per theme plus a full Terminal palette; everything else is derived in `src/index.css`.
Rail and Host list share the sidebar colour; tabs, gutters and status bar sit on the ground.
Work panels are flush, bordered and 10px rounded; they do not float on shadows.
Host identity is an ANSI hue (monogram tile, tab underline); Connection state is green, amber, red.
System UI sans at 13px; mono only where characters must be exact.

rules.name: The Twelve Roles Rule
rules.body: A theme is exactly the twelve `ThemeUi` roles plus a complete Terminal palette, all `#rrggbb`. A new colour need is a role derived in `src/index.css` from those variables, never a literal in a component and never a thirteenth role added to one theme only. Literal hex lives only in `src/theme/themes.ts` and `src/theme/terminal-themes.ts`.

rules.name: The AA Rule
rules.body: Every theme passes WCAG AA (4.5:1), enforced per theme by `src/theme/themes.test.ts`: foreground on ground, surface and raised; muted foreground on surface and ground; primary foreground on primary; Terminal foreground on Terminal background. A theme port that fails is adjusted until it passes, not exempted. Monogram ink is held to 4.6:1 on every tile backing.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Primary marks what is primary, current, checked or focused. It is not decoration, not a heading colour and not a state colour.

rules.name: The State Colour Rule
rules.body: Green means connected, amber means connecting or reconnecting (and pulses), red means disconnected, failed, or host key mismatch. They appear wherever a Host appears (Host row, Host card, tab, status bar) and are used for nothing else. State is never colour alone: an `sr-only` label, tooltip or text names it.

rules.name: The Hue Is Identity Rule
rules.body: A Host's colour is one of six ANSI hues (red, green, yellow, blue, magenta, cyan), a stable FNV-1a hash of its id (`hostHue`), painted only through `--ansi-*` tokens so every theme recolours it. Hue says *which* Host; it never says Connection state.

rules.name: The Mono-Means-Exact Rule
rules.body: Mono is used only where every character matters: the Terminal, addresses, paths, host key fingerprints and key paths, commands quoted in copy. Never for labels, counts or decoration.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: All UI copy is sentence case. No uppercase labels, no letter-spaced small caps. Theme names are proper nouns, shown untranslated.

rules.name: The Shared Row Rule
rules.body: Chrome rows across columns share one height (34px), so the window reads as one grid; a new header in the sidebar or main column takes the same row.

rules.name: The Flush Panel Rule
rules.body: Terminal, File, Home and Settings panels never float: 1px border, ground around them, no shadow. Depth comes from the theme's tonal steps.

rules.name: The Two Shadows Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two shadows, `shadow-panel` and `shadow-overlay`, both derived from the theme. Tailwind's `shadow-xs/sm/md/lg` are not part of the system.

dos: Do style components with semantic tokens only (`bg-background`, `bg-sidebar`, `bg-surface`, `bg-popover`, `bg-muted`, `bg-accent`, `bg-selected`, `text-muted-foreground`, `border`, `ring`, `bg-terminal-background`, `bg-ansi-*`, `text-ansi-*-ink`, `text-success`, `text-warning`, `text-destructive`); derive a new role in `src/index.css` from `--ui-*`.
Do add a theme as a complete `AppTheme` (twelve ui roles plus the full Terminal palette, all `#rrggbb`) and run `src/theme/themes.test.ts`; adjust colours until every AA pair passes.
Do paint a Host's identity only through `hostHue` and `hueClasses` (tile, dot, line), so every theme recolours it.
Do show Connection state wherever a Host appears: green connected, amber connecting (pulsing), red disconnected or host key mismatch, always named in text, `sr-only` or tooltip.
Do keep chrome rows at 34px, panels flush with 6px gutters that are the resize handles, and the status bar at 24px.
Do use the overridden Tailwind sizes (`text-xs` 11.5px, `text-sm` 13px, `text-base` 14px, `text-lg` 15px) and the radius scale (6 / 8 / 10 / 14px).
Do build icon-only controls with `IconButton` and a `label`; give every interactive element a visible `:focus-visible` ring (`ring`, 3px halo).
Do respect `prefers-reduced-motion`: the base layer reduces every animation and transition to near zero.

Do capitalise GLOSSARY.md terms in English copy (Host, Group, Jump host, Connection, Known host, Terminal, Local terminal, File panel, Port forward), write everything else in sentence case, and put all copy behind i18n keys in both locales.
donts: Don't put literal colours, Tailwind palette colours or arbitrary colour values in components; literal hex belongs only in `themes.ts` and `terminal-themes.ts`.
Don't give a theme a colour the Terminal and chrome don't share, or recolour the Terminal without the chrome: one theme paints the whole window.
Don't use primary for decoration, a Host hue for state, or a state colour for identity.
Don't float work panels on shadows, or use shadows other than `shadow-panel` and `shadow-overlay`.
Don't use mono outside the Terminal, addresses, paths, fingerprints and quoted commands.
Don't use uppercase or letter-spaced labels, or set font sizes outside the overridden scale.
Don't reach for a modal first: dialogs are for security confirmations, destructive confirmations and the Host editor.
